title_en: Regulations on the Prevention of Environmental Pollution from Ship Dismantling

articles.content_en: Article 1 These Regulations are formulated for the purpose of preventing environmental pollution from ship breaking, protecting ecological balance, safeguarding human health, and promoting the development of the ship breaking industry.

Article 2 These Regulations shall apply to any unit or individual engaged in shore-based and water-based ship breaking activities within the waters under the jurisdiction of the People's Republic of China.

Article 3 For the purpose of these Regulations, "shore-based ship breaking" means the dismantling of a discarded ship moored at a ship breaking wharf, the dismantling of a discarded ship in a dock, or the dismantling of a discarded ship beached (excluding ship beaching in maritime accidents).
For the purpose of these Regulations, "water-based ship breaking" means the dismantling of a discarded ship entirely on water.

Article 4 The environmental protection department of the people's government at or above the county level shall be responsible for organizing, coordinating, supervising, and inspecting the environmental protection work of the ship breaking industry, and shall take charge of the environmental protection work of shore-based ship breaking outside port waters.
The Harbour Superintendency Administration of the People's Republic of China (including the Harbour and Navigation Superintendency, hereinafter the same) shall take charge of the environmental protection work of water-based ship breaking and ship breaking in the waters of comprehensive ports, and shall assist the environmental protection department in supervising the pollution prevention work of shore-based ship breaking outside port waters.
The national fishery administration and fishery harbour supervision and management department shall take charge of the environmental protection work of ship breaking in fishery harbour waters, be responsible for supervising the impact of ship breaking activities on coastal fishery waters, and upon discovery of any pollution damage accident, shall investigate and handle the matter jointly with the environmental protection department.
The environmental protection department of the military shall take charge of the environmental protection work of ship breaking in military port waters.
The national ocean management department and the water resources protection institutions of major rivers shall, in accordance with the duties determined by the Marine Environment Protection Law of the People's Republic of China and the Water Pollution Prevention and Control Law of the People's Republic of China, assist the competent departments referred to in the preceding paragraphs in supervising the pollution prevention work of ship breaking.
When the environmental protection department of the people's government at or above the county level, the Harbour Superintendency Administration of the People's Republic of China, the national fishery administration and fishery harbour supervision and management department, and the environmental protection department of the military take charge of the environmental protection work of ship breaking in the waters specified in the first, second, third, and fourth paragraphs of this Article, they are hereinafter referred to as the "competent department for supervision of ship breaking pollution."

Article 5 Local people's governments shall, based on need and feasibility and in light of the local characteristics, environmental conditions, and technical capabilities, make overall plans and establish ship breaking yards in a reasonable manner.
No ship breaking yard shall be established in sources of drinking water, seawater desalination intake points, salt fields, important fishery waters, bathing beaches, scenic and historic areas, or other areas requiring special protection.

Article 6 For the establishment of a ship breaking yard, an environmental impact report (form) must be prepared. The contents shall include: the geographical location of the ship breaking yard, the surrounding environmental conditions, the scale and conditions of ship breaking, the ship breaking process, pollution prevention measures, expected prevention and control results, etc. No ship breaking yard that has not undergone environmental impact assessment according to law shall commence construction.
Before approving the environmental impact report (form), the environmental protection department shall seek opinions from the relevant departments.

Article 7 The competent department for supervision of ship breaking pollution shall have the right to inspect the ship breaking activities of a ship breaking unit, and the unit under inspection must truthfully report the situation and provide necessary materials.
The competent department for supervision of ship breaking pollution shall have the obligation to keep confidential the technical and business secrets of the unit under inspection.

Article 8 A ship breaking unit that seriously pollutes the environment shall be ordered to rectify within a specified time limit.
The rectification within a specified time limit for a ship breaking unit shall be proposed by the competent department for supervision of ship breaking pollution, and shall be submitted through the environmental protection department that approved the environmental impact report (form) to the people's government at the same level for decision.
Article 9 A ship breaking unit shall improve its environmental protection rules and regulations, and shall earnestly organize their implementation.

Article 10 A ship breaking unit must equip or install such facilities as oil containment devices, waste oil receiving equipment, oily wastewater receiving and treatment facilities or equipment, and waste recovery and disposal sites as are necessary for preventing ship breaking pollution, and may only commence ship breaking after the environmental protection department that approved the environmental impact report (form) has inspected and accepted the said facilities and issued an acceptance certificate.

Article 11 Before dismantling a discarded ship, a ship breaking unit must remove flammable, explosive, and toxic substances; close sea valves and seal pipelines that may cause the spillage of oily wastewater. Wastes such as garbage, residual oil, waste oil, oil sludge, oily wastewater, and flammable and explosive articles must be transported to shore for centralized treatment, and treatment methods involving seepage pits or seepage wells shall not be used.
Before dismantling a discarded oil tanker, operations such as tank washing, pollutant discharge, tank cleaning, and explosion-proof testing must be carried out.

Article 12 Any unit or individual engaged in water-based ship breaking operations must take effective measures in advance to strictly prevent the spread of oil and other floatable substances that may overflow or fall into the water.
During water-based ship breaking operations, once oil or other floatable substances overflow or fall into the water, they must be promptly collected and treated.

Article 13 The discharge of tank washing water, ballast water, and bilge water must comply with the discharge standards prescribed by the State and local authorities; the discharge of untreated tank washing water, ballast water, and bilge water must also be approved by the competent department for supervision of ship breaking pollution.
Upon receiving a report from a ship breaking unit applying for the discharge of untreated tank washing water, ballast water, and bilge water, the competent department for supervision of ship breaking pollution shall promptly handle and approve the matter in a timely manner.

Article 14 Dismantled ship parts or wastes shall not be dumped or stored in water; ship parts or wastes carrying pollutants are strictly prohibited from entering water bodies. Ship bottoms and oil tanks that have not been thoroughly cleaned must be towed to shore for dismantling.
Calcium carbide slag and its wastewater generated from ship breaking operations must be collected and treated and shall not flow into water bodies.
After the dismantling of a ship is completed, the unit or individual engaged in ship breaking shall promptly clean up the ship breaking site.

Article 15 When a ship breaking pollution damage accident occurs, the ship breaking unit or individual must immediately take measures to eliminate or control the pollution, and shall promptly report to the competent department for supervision of ship breaking pollution.
After the occurrence of a pollution damage accident, the ship breaking unit must submit a "Pollution Accident Report" to the competent department for supervision of ship breaking pollution, reporting the cause of the pollution, the course of events, the quantity of pollutants discharged, the rescue measures taken, the pollution damage consequences already caused and likely to be caused, etc., and shall accept investigation and handling.

Article 16 After a ship breaking unit is closed or relocated, it must promptly clean up the pollutants left at the original site, and the competent department for supervision of ship breaking pollution shall inspect and accept the cleanup.

Article 17 Where any of the following circumstances occurs in violation of these Regulations, the competent department for supervision of ship breaking pollution shall, in addition to ordering correction within a specified time limit, also impose a fine of not less than 10,000 yuan but not more than 100,000 yuan, depending on the circumstances:
(1) a pollution damage accident occurs, and the party neither reports to the competent department for supervision of ship breaking pollution nor takes measures to eliminate or control the pollution;
(2) a discarded oil tanker is dismantled without undergoing tank washing, pollutant discharge, tank cleaning, and explosion-proof testing; or
(3) pollutants are discharged or discarded arbitrarily causing serious pollution.
Where a ship breaking yard is established and ship breaking is carried out without authorization in an area specified in paragraph 2 of Article 5 in violation of these Regulations, the people's government at or above the county level shall, in accordance with the principle of graded management, order closure or relocation within a specified time limit.
Where a ship breaking yard commences construction without authorization without undergoing environmental impact assessment according to law, the matter shall be penalized in accordance with the provisions of the Environmental Protection Law of the People's Republic of China.

Article 19 All fines shall be turned over to the State treasury.
The imposition of a fine on a ship breaking unit or individual shall not relieve it or him from the performance of the obligations prescribed in these Regulations; where pollution hazards have been caused, the hazards must be promptly eliminated.

Article 20 A ship breaking unit that fails to complete the rectification task within the specified time limit may, depending on the harmful consequences caused, be ordered to suspend operations for rectification or be closed down.
The suspension of operations for rectification or closure of a ship breaking unit referred to in the preceding paragraph shall be decided by the people's government that made the decision on rectification within a specified time limit. The suspension of operations for rectification or closure of a ship breaking unit directly under a relevant department of the State Council shall be approved by the environmental protection department of the State Council jointly with the relevant department.

Article 21 The person in charge and the directly responsible person of a ship breaking unit who bear responsibility for causing pollution damage consequences or who commit the acts specified in item (1) of Article 18 may, depending on the circumstances, be given disciplinary sanctions by the unit to which they belong or by the competent authority at a higher level.

Article 22 If a party is dissatisfied with the decision on administrative penalty, it may file a lawsuit with the People's Court within 15 days from the date of receipt of the notice of the penalty decision; if no lawsuit is filed within the time limit and the decision is not complied with, the competent department that made the penalty decision shall apply to the People's Court for compulsory execution.

Article 23 Any unit or individual that has directly suffered damage from ship breaking pollution shall have the right to claim compensation for losses from the party that caused the pollution damage. The party that caused the pollution damage shall be liable to compensate for the losses of the unit or individual that has directly suffered harm.
A dispute over the liability for compensation and the amount of compensation may, upon the request of the parties, be handled by the competent department for supervision of ship breaking pollution; if a party is dissatisfied with the handling decision, it may file a lawsuit with the People's Court.
A party may also directly file a lawsuit with the People's Court.

Article 24 Any unit or individual that has directly suffered damage from ship breaking pollution and claims compensation for losses shall submit a "Pollution Claim Report." The report shall include the following:
(1) the time, place, scope, and object of the damage suffered from ship breaking pollution, as well as the meteorological and hydrological conditions at the time;
(2) a detailed list of losses suffered from ship breaking pollution, including the names, quantities, unit prices, calculation methods, etc.; and
(3) the expert evaluation from the relevant monitoring department.

Article 25 Where a pollution damage is caused by irresistible natural disasters and cannot be avoided despite the timely adoption of preventive and rescue measures, the liability for compensation shall be exempted.

Article 26 Units and individuals that report or expose the concealment or false reporting of pollution damage accidents by ship breaking units, and those that actively take measures to stop or mitigate pollution damage, shall be given commendation and rewards.

Article 27 Where a staff member of the competent department for supervision of ship breaking pollution neglects his duty, abuses his power, or engages in malpractice for personal gain, he shall be given disciplinary sanctions by the unit to which he belongs or by the competent authority at a higher level; if the act causes major losses to the interests of the State and the people and constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.
Article 28 These Regulations shall come into force as of June 1, 1988.
